topics.title: Author and manage workflows
topics.summary: Official exam domain 1 (20–25% of questions, tied for the largest domain). Covers triggers/events, workflow structure (jobs, steps, matrix, YAML anchors, contexts/expressions), and managing execution/outputs (caching, artifacts, job summaries).

subtopics.title: Configure workflow triggers and events
subtopics.summary: Scheduled (cron), manual (workflow_dispatch), webhook, and repository events; choosing scope/permissions/events for automation; defining and validating workflow_dispatch inputs (types, required, defaults); passing inputs to reusable workflows via workflow_call with inputs and secrets mapping.

subtopics.title: Design and implement workflow structure
subtopics.summary: Jobs, steps, and conditional logic (if:); job dependencies (needs:); workflow commands and environment variables; service containers (services:) for databases/queues with ports and health checks; strategy/matrix for job variations (OS, runtime versions) with include/exclude, fail-fast, max-parallel, and cost/perf optimization; runner image changes (Ubuntu 20.04 deprecation, Windows Server 2025 migration); YAML anchors/aliases (&, *, merge <<) to reuse mappings/steps; predefined contexts (github, runner, env, vars, secrets, inputs, matrix, needs, strategy, job, steps) and immutable actions/version pinning; expression evaluation with ${{ }} — static (parse-time) vs runtime, and preventing secret leakage; editor tooling (VS Code Actions extension, YAML schema/IntelliSense).

subtopics.title: Manage workflow execution and outputs
subtopics.summary: Caching and artifact management, plus retention policies applied via REST APIs (logs, artifacts, workflow runs) at org/repo level; passing data between jobs/steps (artifacts, outputs, GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_OUTPUT environment files, reusable workflow outputs); generating rich Markdown job summaries with GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (test results, coverage, links); workflow status badges and environment protections.

topics.title: Consume and troubleshoot workflows
topics.summary: Official exam domain 2 (15–20% of questions). Covers interpreting workflow behavior/logs, accessing artifacts and logs via UI/API, and understanding the template ecosystem (starter workflows, reusable workflows, composite actions).

subtopics.title: Interpret workflow behavior and results
subtopics.summary: Identifying workflow triggers and their effects from configuration and logs; diagnosing failed workflow runs using logs and run history; expanding and interpreting YAML anchors, aliases, and merged mappings when analyzing workflow configuration; interpreting matrix expansions, correlating job names to matrix axes, analyzing failures across variants, and selectively rerunning individual matrix jobs.

subtopics.title: Access workflow artifacts and logs
subtopics.summary: Locating workflows, logs, and artifacts in the UI and via the REST API; downloading and managing workflow artifacts.

subtopics.title: Use and manage workflow templates
subtopics.summary: Consuming organization-level and reusable workflows, including non-public organization workflow templates; using starter workflows (public and private/non-public templates), customizing and adapting them; distinguishing starter workflows (copy scaffold, independent after creation) vs reusable workflows (central versioned definition invoked via workflow_call) vs composite actions (encapsulated step logic); contrasting disabling vs deleting workflows.

topics.title: Author and maintain actions
topics.summary: Official exam domain 3 (15–20% of questions). Covers creating and troubleshooting custom actions (JavaScript, Docker, composite), required metadata/structure, and distributing/versioning actions.

subtopics.title: Create and troubleshoot custom actions
subtopics.summary: Identifying and implementing action types (JavaScript, Docker, composite); understanding the immutable actions rollout on hosted runners and its implications for version pinning and registry sources; troubleshooting action execution and errors.

subtopics.title: Define action structure and metadata
subtopics.summary: Specifying required files, directory structure, and metadata (action.yml/action.yaml: name, description, inputs, outputs, runs); implementing workflow commands within actions.

subtopics.title: Distribute and maintain actions
subtopics.summary: Selecting distribution models (public, private, marketplace); publishing actions to the GitHub Marketplace; applying versioning and release strategies (major version tags vs full commit SHAs).

topics.title: Manage GitHub Actions for the enterprise
topics.summary: Official exam domain 4 (20–25% of questions, tied for the largest domain). Covers governing actions/workflows org-wide, managing runners at scale (hosted and self-hosted), and scoping encrypted secrets/variables.

subtopics.title: Distribute and govern actions and workflows
subtopics.summary: Defining and managing reusable components and templates; controlling access to actions and workflows within the enterprise; configuring organizational use policies (allow/deny lists).

subtopics.title: Manage runners at scale
subtopics.summary: Configuring and monitoring GitHub-hosted and self-hosted runners; applying IP allow lists and networking settings; managing runner groups and troubleshooting runner issues; identifying preinstalled software/tool versions on GitHub-hosted runners (image release notes, toolcache) and installing additional software at runtime (setup-* actions, package managers, caching, container images, custom self-hosted images).

subtopics.title: Manage encrypted secrets and variables
subtopics.summary: Defining and scoping encrypted secrets and variables at the organization, repository, and environment levels; accessing and using secrets/variables in workflows and actions; managing secrets and variables programmatically via REST APIs.

topics.title: Secure and optimize automation
topics.summary: Official exam domain 5 (10–15% of questions, the smallest domain but dense with distinct exam-relevant facts). Covers security best practices (OIDC, GITHUB_TOKEN, SHA pinning, attestations) and performance/cost optimization.

subtopics.title: Implement security best practices
subtopics.summary: Environment protections and approval gates; identifying and using trustworthy actions from the Marketplace; mitigating script injection (sanitize/validate inputs, least-privilege permissions, avoid untrusted data in run:, proper shell quoting, prefer vetted actions over inline scripts); GITHUB_TOKEN lifecycle (ephemeral, scoped), configuring granular permissions, contrasting with PAT, restricting write scopes; using OIDC (id-token permission) for cloud provider federation to eliminate long-lived cloud secrets; pinning third-party actions to full commit SHAs, aligning with immutable actions enforcement, avoiding floating @main/@v* without justification; enforcing action usage policies (org/repo allow/deny lists, required reviewers for unverified actions); generating and verifying artifact attestations/provenance (SLSA, build metadata) and integrating into deployment verification.

subtopics.title: Optimize workflow performance and cost
subtopics.summary: Configuring caching and artifact retention for efficiency, including retention policies applied programmatically via REST APIs; recommending strategies for scaling and optimizing workflows (matrix size, runner sizing, concurrency, self-hosted vs hosted trade-offs).

topics.title: Case study: applied review across your own repos
topics.summary: Exam-style application of all five domains, anchored in projects you've already built — massirr/StudyApp's gh aw agentic workflow and massirr/skills-deploy-to-azure-1's Azure/GHCR CI/CD pipeline. Good final review the night before the exam.

subtopics.title: Case study: StudyApp gh aw agentic workflow
subtopics.summary: The repo-status.md workflow, copilot-setup-steps.yml, .github/agents/, .github/mcp.json, and secrets setup (fine-grained PAT via gh aw secrets set COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN) map directly to exam topics: workflow triggers/scheduling, secrets scoping, GITHUB_TOKEN vs PAT, troubleshooting failed runs from logs, and model-pinning as a workflow input/config choice.

subtopics.title: Case study: skills-deploy-to-azure-1 Azure/GHCR pipeline
subtopics.summary: The Node.js build → Docker image → GHCR push → Azure Web App deploy pipeline maps to exam topics: service containers vs. Docker build/push actions, classic PAT (CR_PAT) vs fine-grained PAT for GHCR, secrets (CR_PAT, Azure credentials JSON) scoped at repo/environment level, and where OIDC federation could replace the stored Azure service-principal secret entirely.

questions.prompt: You define a workflow_dispatch input `environment` (type: choice, required: true, no default). Someone triggers the workflow via the REST API without supplying `environment`. What happens?

options.label: The API request is rejected with a validation error and no workflow run is created, since required inputs must be supplied
GitHub automatically defaults it to the first choice option
The step resolves inputs.environment to an empty string and the job continues
The run queues indefinitely waiting for someone to supply the missing input

questions.explanation: Required workflow_dispatch inputs without a default must be supplied. Triggering via the API without one causes the request itself to fail validation — no run is ever created.

questions.prompt: A reusable workflow declares `on: workflow_call: inputs: environment: {required: true, type: string} secrets: DEPLOY_TOKEN: {required: true}`. The caller workflow's job uses `secrets: inherit`. What does `secrets: inherit` do?

options.label: Passes only the DEPLOY_TOKEN secret declared in the called workflow's inputs
Passes every secret available to the calling workflow into the called workflow, without listing them individually
Automatically generates a new short-lived secret scoped to just this call
Has no effect unless the called workflow also sets secrets: inherit

questions.explanation: secrets: inherit passes all of the calling workflow's secrets down to the called workflow, as an alternative to explicitly mapping each secret under a secrets: block.
